blocks.markdown: **Version caution.** The syllabus parenthetical refers to RA Nos. 9160, 9194, 10365, and 10927, but RA No. 11521 (2021) further amended the AMLA. This lesson flags later amendments where they change important rules, including the covered-person/transaction framework and freezing powers. Do not treat a historical version of a section as current merely because it appears in the original RA 9160.

RA 9160, Section 2, as amended by RA 11521, declares State policy to **protect and preserve the integrity and confidentiality of bank accounts** and to **ensure that the Philippines shall not be used as a money laundering site** for the proceeds of any unlawful activity. Consistent with its foreign policy, the State extends cooperation in transnational money-laundering investigations and prosecutions, as well as in implementing **targeted financial sanctions** related to proliferation of weapons of mass destruction, terrorism, and financing of terrorism under UN Security Council resolutions.

In plain English: the State wants to **protect legitimate banking privacy while stopping criminals from hiding illegal proceeds** in the financial system. These goals work together — privacy is important, but it is not absolute when a lawful AMLA process applies. The 2021 amendment also connects the AMLA to targeted financial sanctions for terrorism and proliferation financing.

**Key distinction:** the AMLA does not make every unusual transaction illegal. It creates **reporting, investigation, and provisional-remedy mechanisms**. Criminal liability still depends on the applicable legal elements and proof.
**Issue-spotting reminder:** ask what version of the statute applies on the transaction date. Later amendments may change definitions, thresholds, covered persons, and procedure.

description: State policy under AMLA Section 2: banking privacy balanced with anti-money-laundering enforcement and international cooperation.
title: Policy: AMLA Section 2
